# relaybot

> Dispatch Codex or Claude Code from a chat bot or personal agent such as Grok Bot: run the chosen CLI on your own computer, get a webhook callback when the coding agent finishes, fails, or needs approval, and resume the same session afterwards. Codex app-server threads appear in the desktop. Users can send `/handoff` to open the current Codex or Claude session on their desktop.

The personal agent keeps the context and writes the full prompt; the user picks the coding agent explicitly; tasks use the selected CLI’s local account; sessions are managed for them.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what it solves, when to use it, status
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): layout, config keys, self-check commands
- [Install for agents](docs/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md): end-to-end install and verification steps
- [Install](docs/INSTALL.md): manual install and configuration reference
- [Usage](docs/USAGE.md): /codex, /claude and the shared /relaybot-setup
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): app-server flow, projectId, desktop refresh, hooks, webhook event contract

## Skills

- [skills/codex/SKILL.md](skills/codex/SKILL.md): /codex or /claude, dispatch a task and handle events
- [skills/claude/SKILL.md](skills/claude/SKILL.md) routes /claude to the codex skill's dispatch and resume instructions with `claude-run`.
- [skills/handoff/SKILL.md](skills/handoff/SKILL.md) opens the current task on the desktop when the user sends /handoff.
- [skills/auto-sync/SKILL.md](skills/auto-sync/SKILL.md) toggles a single run’s desktop update. Handoff schedules the update by default on macOS.
- [skills/relaybot-setup/SKILL.md](skills/relaybot-setup/SKILL.md) checks Codex and Claude Code independently and tests their shared webhook.
